bookInfo.author: Xue Juzheng et al.

title.zh: 卷一百三十八 外國列傳二: 吐蕃 回鶻 高麗 渤海靺鞨 黑水靺鞨 新羅 党項 昆明部落 于闐 占城 牂牁蠻
title.en: Volume 138: Foreign States Biographies 2: Tubo, Huihu, Goryeo, Bohai Tungusic Tribes, Heishui Tungusic Tribes, Silla, Tangut, Kunming Tribes, Yutian, Champa, Zangkeman
title.raw: 卷一百三十八 外國列傳二: 吐蕃 回鶻 高麗 渤海靺鞨 黑水靺鞨 新羅 党項 昆明部落 于闐 占城 牂牁蠻 Volume 138: Foreign States Biographies 2: Tubo, Huihu, Goryeo, Bohai Tungusic Tribes, Heishui Tungusic Tribes, Silla, Tangut, Kunming Tribes, Yutian, Champa, Zangkeman

sentences.zh: 吐蕃 回鶻 高麗 渤海靺鞨 黑水靺鞨 新羅 党項 昆明部落 于闐 占城 牂牁蠻

translations.literal: Tubo, Huihu, Goryeo, Bohai Mohe, Heishui Mohe, Silla, Tangut, Kunming tribes, Yutian, Champa, Zangke Man.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo, the Uyghurs, Goryeo, the Bohai Mohe, the Heishui Mohe, Silla, the Tangut, the Kunming tribes, Yutian, Champa, and the Zangke Man.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃，本漢西羌之地，或雲南涼禿發利鹿孤之後，其子孫以禿發爲國號，語訛爲吐蕃。

translations.literal: Tubo was originally the land of the Western Qiang in Han times; some say it was the descendants of Tufa Lilugu of Southern Liang, whose descendants took Tufa as their state name, which in speech was corrupted into Tubo.
translations.idiomatic: The Tubo realm had originally been the territory of the Western Qiang in Han times. Some held that its people were descended from Tufa Lilugu of Southern Liang and that their descendants had taken Tufa as the name of their state—a name that, in common speech, was corrupted into Tubo.

sentences.zh: 國人號其主爲贊普，置大論、小論以理國事。

translations.literal: The people called their ruler zanpu and appointed great and minor lun officials to manage state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The people addressed their sovereign as zanpu and appointed great and minor councillors to administer the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 其俗隨畜牧無常居，然亦有城郭，都城號邏些城。

translations.literal: Their custom was to follow pastoral herding without fixed dwellings, yet they also had walled towns; the capital was called Luoxie City.
translations.idiomatic: By custom they followed their herds and had no fixed abode, yet they also maintained walled settlements; their capital was known as Luoxie City.

sentences.zh: 不知節候，以麥熟爲歲首。

translations.literal: They did not know the seasons and took the ripening of wheat as the start of the year.
translations.idiomatic: Unacquainted with the calendrical seasons, they reckoned the ripening of wheat as the beginning of the year.

sentences.zh: 唐時屢爲邊患。

translations.literal: In Tang times they repeatedly became a border menace.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang they were a recurring scourge along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 初，唐分天下爲十道，河西、隴右三十三州，涼州最爲大鎮。

translations.literal: At first the Tang divided the realm into ten circuits; Hexi and Longyou had thirty-three prefectures, and Liangzhou was the greatest stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the Tang had divided the empire into ten circuits. Hexi and Longyou comprised thirty-three prefectures, of which Liangzhou was the principal stronghold.

sentences.zh: 天寶置八監，牧馬三十萬，又置都護以控制之。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era eight pasture commissions were established with three hundred thousand horses under herd, and a protector-general was also installed to control them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign eight pasture commissions were set up to pasture three hundred thousand horses, and a protector-general was appointed to keep them under control.

sentences.zh: 安祿山之亂，肅宗在靈武，悉召河西戍卒收復兩京，吐蕃乘虛取河西、隴右，華人百萬皆陷於吐蕃。

translations.literal: In An Lushan's rebellion, when Emperor Suzong was at Lingwu, he summoned all Hexi garrison troops to recover the two capitals; Tubo seized the opportunity and took Hexi and Longyou, and a million Chinese subjects all fell under Tubo.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion and Emperor Suzong was at Lingwu, he called up every soldier garrisoned in Hexi to retake the two capitals. Tubo seized the moment, overran Hexi and Longyou, and more than a million Chinese subjects were lost to Tubo rule.

sentences.zh: 開成時，朝廷嘗遣使至西域，見甘、涼、瓜、沙等州城邑如故，陷吐蕃之人見唐使者旌節，夾道迎呼涕泣曰：「皇帝猶念陷吐蕃生靈否？」

translations.literal: In the Kaicheng era the court once sent envoys to the Western Regions and saw that the cities of Gan, Liang, Gua, Sha, and other prefectures remained as before; people who had fallen to Tubo, seeing the Tang envoy's banners and credentials, lined the roads to welcome them, weeping and calling out, "Does the Emperor still remember the living souls lost to Tubo?"
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaicheng reign the court once dispatched envoys to the Western Regions. They found the cities of Gan, Liang, Gua, Sha, and the other prefectures still standing as before. When those who had been lost to Tubo saw the Tang envoy's banners of office, they lined the road to greet him, weeping and crying, "Does the Son of Heaven still remember the people trapped under Tubo?"

sentences.zh: 其人皆天寶中陷吐蕃者子孫，其語言小訛，而衣服未改。

translations.literal: These people were all descendants of those who had fallen to Tubo in the Tianbao era; their speech was slightly altered, but their clothing had not changed.
translations.idiomatic: They were all descendants of people who had been lost to Tubo in the Tianbao years. Their speech had shifted slightly, but they still wore the same dress as before.

sentences.zh: 至五代時，吐蕃已微弱，回鶻、党項諸羌夷分侵其地，而不有其人民。

translations.literal: By the Five Dynasties period Tubo had already grown weak; the Huihu, Tangut, and various Qiang and Yi peoples divided and encroached on its lands without holding its populace.
translations.idiomatic: By the Five Dynasties Tubo had already waned. The Uyghurs, Tangut, and other Qiang and frontier peoples carved up and raided its territory yet did not truly hold its people.

sentences.zh: 值中國衰亂，不能撫有，惟甘、涼、瓜、沙四州常自通於中國。

translations.literal: As China fell into decline and disorder and could not govern them, only the four prefectures of Gan, Liang, Gua, and Sha regularly maintained their own contact with China.
translations.idiomatic: With the central realm in turmoil and unable to assert control, only Gan, Liang, Gua, and Sha—the four prefectures—continued to keep contact with China on their own.

sentences.zh: 甘州爲回鶻牙帳，而涼、瓜、沙三州將吏猶稱唐官，數來請命。

translations.literal: Ganzhou served as the Huihu royal encampment, while the officers of Liang, Gua, and Sha still styled themselves Tang officials and came repeatedly to request commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Prefecture became the seat of the Uyghur royal camp, but the commanders and clerks of Liang, Gua, and Sha still called themselves Tang officials and came again and again to seek imperial appointment.

sentences.zh: 自梁太祖時，常以靈武節度使兼領河西節度，而觀察甘、肅、威等州，然雖有其名，而涼州自立守將。

translations.literal: From the time of Emperor Taizu of Liang, the military governor of Lingwu was usually also made military governor of Hexi and overseer of Gan, Su, Wei, and other prefectures; yet though the title existed, Liangzhou maintained its own defending commander.
translations.idiomatic: From the reign of the Liang founder onward, the military governor of Lingwu was routinely given concurrent command of Hexi and oversight of Gan, Su, Wei, and neighboring prefectures. In name the post existed, but Liangzhou kept its own defending commander.

sentences.zh: 唐長興四年，涼州留後孫超遣大將拓拔承謙及僧道士耆老楊通信等至京師，明宗拜孫超節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing of Later Tang, Liangzhou acting governor Sun Chao sent the great general Tuoba Chengqian and the monk, Daoist, and elder Yang Tongxin and others to the capital; Emperor Mingzong appointed Sun Chao military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Later Tang Changxing era, Sun Chao, acting governor of Liangzhou, sent his senior general Tuoba Chengqian together with monks, Daoists, and elders led by Yang Tongxin to the capital. Emperor Mingzong then invested Sun Chao as military governor.

sentences.zh: 清泰元年，留後李文謙來請命。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingtai, acting governor Li Wenqian came to request a commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingtai, acting governor Li Wenqian came to seek imperial appointment.

sentences.zh: 後數年，涼州人逐出文謙，靈武馮暉遣牙將吳繼興代文謙爲留後，是時天福七年。

translations.literal: Several years later the people of Liangzhou drove out Wenqian; Feng Hui of Lingwu sent his adjutant Wu Jixing to replace Wenqian as acting governor—this was in the seventh year of Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later the people of Liangzhou expelled Wenqian. Feng Hui of Lingwu dispatched his adjutant Wu Jixing to replace him as acting governor. This was in the seventh year of Tianfu.

sentences.zh: 明年，晉高祖遣涇州押牙陳延暉齎詔書安撫涼州，涼州人共劫留延暉，立以爲刺史。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Gaozu of Jin sent Chen Yanhui, adjutant of Jingzhou, bearing an edict to pacify Liangzhou; the people of Liangzhou together detained Yanhui by force and installed him as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Emperor Gaozu of Jin sent Chen Yanhui, adjutant of Jing Prefecture, with an edict to reassure Liangzhou. The people of Liangzhou seized him and made him their prefect.

sentences.zh: 至漢隱帝時，涼州留後折逋嘉施來請命，漢即以爲節度使。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Yindi of Han, Liangzhou acting governor Zhebo Jiashi came to request a commission, and Han immediately appointed him military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yindi of Later Han, Zhebo Jiashi, acting governor of Liangzhou, came to seek appointment, and the Han court at once made him military governor.

sentences.zh: 嘉施，土豪也。

translations.literal: Jiashi was a local strongman.
translations.idiomatic: Jiashi was a local magnate.

sentences.zh: 周廣順二年，嘉施遣人市馬京師。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangshun of Zhou, Jiashi sent men to buy horses in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangshun under the Zhou, Jiashi sent agents to purchase horses in the capital.

sentences.zh: 是時樞密使王峻用事，峻故人申師厚者，少起盜賊，爲兗州牙將，與峻相友善。

translations.literal: At that time Privy Councilor Wang Jun held power; Jun's old acquaintance Shen Shihou had risen from banditry in youth, became adjutant of Yanzhou, and was on friendly terms with Jun.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Privy Councilor Wang Jun dominated the court. An old friend of his, Shen Shihou, had begun life as a bandit and later became adjutant of Yan Prefecture; he and Jun were close.

sentences.zh: 後峻貴，師厚弊衣蓬首，日候峻出，馬前訴以饑寒，峻未有以發。

translations.literal: Later, when Jun became eminent, Shihou in ragged clothes and unkempt hair daily waited for Jun to go out and pleaded before his horse of hunger and cold; Jun had no way to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: After Jun rose to power, Shihou would appear in ragged clothes with hair in disarray, wait each day for Jun to leave his residence, and plead before his horse of hunger and cold. Jun had no means to help him.

sentences.zh: 而嘉施等來請帥，峻即建言，涼州深入夷狄，中國未嘗命吏，請帥募府率供奉官能往者。

translations.literal: When Jiashi and others came to request a commander, Jun at once proposed that Liangzhou lay deep among the barbarians and China had never appointed officials there, and asked that a commander be recruited from palace attendants able to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiashi and his party came to request a commander, Jun immediately proposed that Liangzhou lay far within barbarian territory and that the central court had never stationed officials there. He asked that a commander be recruited from among palace attendants willing to go.

sentences.zh: 月餘，無應募者，乃奏起師厚爲左衛將軍，已而拜河西節度使。

translations.literal: After more than a month with no volunteers, he memorialized to recall Shihou as Left Guard General, and shortly afterward Shihou was appointed military governor of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month without a single volunteer, he memorialized to recall Shihou as general of the Left Guard, and soon afterward Shihou was appointed military governor of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 師厚至涼州，奏薦押牙副使崔虎心、陽妃谷首領沈念般等，及中國留人子孫王廷翰、溫崇樂、劉少英爲將吏，又自安國鎮至涼州立三州以控扼諸羌，用其酋豪爲刺史。

translations.literal: When Shihou reached Liangzhou he memorialized recommending adjutant deputy commissioner Cui Huxin, Yangfei Valley chieftain Shen Nianban, and others, and the descendants of Chinese who had remained—Wang Tinghan, Wen Chongle, and Liu Shaoying—as officers; he also established three prefectures from Anguo Town to Liangzhou to control the various Qiang, appointing their chieftains as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Liangzhou, Shihou recommended adjutant deputy commissioner Cui Huxin, the Yangfei Valley chieftain Shen Nianban, and others, together with Wang Tinghan, Wen Chongle, and Liu Shaoying—descendants of Chinese who had stayed behind—as officers. He also set up three prefectures from Anguo Town to Liangzhou to hold the Qiang in check, installing their chieftains as prefects.

sentences.zh: 然涼州夷夏雜處，師厚小人，不能撫有，至世宗時，師厚留其子而逃歸，涼州遂絕於中國。

translations.literal: Yet Liangzhou was a mixed land of barbarians and Chinese; Shihou was a petty man and could not govern it. By the time of Emperor Shizong, Shihou left his son behind and fled back, and Liangzhou was thereafter cut off from China.
translations.idiomatic: But Liangzhou was a mixed region of barbarians and Chinese, and Shihou, a man of small character, could not hold it. By Emperor Shizong's reign he abandoned his son and fled home, and Liangzhou was lost to the central realm thereafter.

sentences.zh: 獨瓜、沙二州，終五代常來。

translations.literal: Only Gua and Sha, the two prefectures, came regularly throughout the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Only Gua and Sha continued to send envoys throughout the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 沙州，梁開平中，有節度使張奉，自號「金山白衣天子」。

translations.literal: In Sha Prefecture, during Kaiping of Liang, there was military governor Zhang Feng, who styled himself "White-Robed Son of Heaven of Golden Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: At Sha Prefecture, during the Liang Kaiping era, military governor Zhang Feng styled himself "the White-Robed Son of Heaven of Golden Mountain."

sentences.zh: 至唐莊宗時，回鶻來朝，沙州留後曹義金亦遣使附回鶻以來，莊宗拜義金爲歸義軍節度使、瓜沙等州觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang, when the Huihu came to court, Sha Prefecture acting governor Cao Yijin also sent envoys attached to the Huihu mission; Zhuangzong appointed Yijin military governor of the Army of Returning Allegiance and commissioner for observation and disposition of Gua, Sha, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang, when the Uyghurs came to court, Cao Yijin, acting governor of Sha Prefecture, sent envoys along with the Uyghur mission. Zhuangzong appointed Yijin military governor of the Army of Returning Allegiance and commissioner overseeing Gua, Sha, and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 晉天福五年，義金卒，子元德立。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu of Jin, Yijin died and his son Yuande succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianfu under Jin, Yijin died and his son Yuande succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 至七年，沙州曹元忠、瓜州曹元深皆遣使來。

translations.literal: By the seventh year, Cao Yuanzhong of Sha and Cao Yuanshen of Gua both sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Cao Yuanzhong of Sha and Cao Yuanshen of Gua each dispatched envoys.

sentences.zh: 周世宗時，又以元忠爲歸義軍節度使，元恭爲瓜州團練使。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Shizong of Zhou, Yuanzhong was again made military governor of the Army of Returning Allegiance and Yuangong regimental trainer of Gua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong of Zhou, Yuanzhong was again appointed military governor of the Army of Returning Allegiance and Yuangong regimental commissioner of Gua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其所貢碙砂、羚羊角、波斯錦、安西白絺、金星礬、大鵬砂、眊褐、玉團，皆因其來者以名見，而其卒立世次，史皆失其紀。

translations.literal: Their tribute of ammoniac, antelope horn, Persian brocade, Anxi white silk, golden-star alum, great peng sand, mao-brown cloth, and jade balls—all were named as they came; but their deaths, successions, and generations are all lost in the records.
translations.idiomatic: They presented ammoniac, antelope horn, Persian brocade, Anxi white silk, golden-star alum, great peng sand, mao-brown cloth, and jade balls—each item recorded as it arrived—but the chronology of their deaths and successions has been lost to history.

sentences.zh: 而吐蕃不見於梁世。

translations.literal: Tubo was not seen in the Liang period.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo sent no missions during the Liang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 唐天成三年，回鶻王仁裕來朝，吐蕃亦遣使附以來，自此數至中國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng of Tang, Huihu King Renyu came to court and Tubo also sent envoys attached to them; from then on they came repeatedly to China.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiancheng under Later Tang, the Uyghur king Renyu came to court, and Tubo sent envoys along with his mission. Thereafter they came to the central realm on numerous occasions.

sentences.zh: 明宗嘗御端明殿見其使者，問其牙帳所居，曰：「西去涇州二千里。」

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong once received their envoys in the Hall of Illuminated Clarity and asked where their royal encampment lay; they replied, "Two thousand li west of Jingzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong once received their envoys in the Hall of Illuminated Clarity and asked where their royal camp stood. They answered, "Two thousand li west of Jing Prefecture."

sentences.zh: 明宗賜以虎皮，人一張，皆披以拜，委身宛轉，落其氈帽，發亂如蓬，明宗及左右皆大笑。

translations.literal: Mingzong bestowed tiger pelts, one per man; all draped them to bow, twisting their bodies, and their felt caps fell off, hair disheveled like tangled hemp; Mingzong and those beside him all laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong gave each man a tiger pelt. They draped the pelts over their shoulders to bow, writhing as they did so until their felt caps fell off and their hair spilled out like a tangled broom. Mingzong and everyone around him burst into laughter.

sentences.zh: 至漢隱帝時，猶來朝，後遂不復至，史亦失其君世雲。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Yindi of Han they still came to court, but afterward they came no more, and the histories also lose track of their rulers' generations.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yindi of Later Han they still came to court, but afterward they ceased coming altogether, and the histories no longer record their royal succession.

sentences.zh: 回鶻，其先匈奴之種也。

translations.literal: The Huihu were originally of Xiongnu stock.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs were descended from the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 後魏時，號爲鐵勒，亦名回紇。

translations.literal: In Northern Wei times they were called Tiele and also named Huihe.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Wei they were known as the Tiele and also as the Huihe.

sentences.zh: 唐元和四年，本國可汗遣使上言，改爲回鶻，義取迴旋搏擊，如鶻之迅捷也。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe of Tang, their khan sent envoys to petition that the name be changed to Huihu, taking the sense of wheeling and striking swiftly like a gyrfalcon.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanhe, their khan petitioned through envoys to change the name to Huihu, meaning to wheel and strike as swiftly as a gyrfalcon.

sentences.zh: 本牙在天德西北婆陵水上，距京師八千餘里。

translations.literal: Their original royal camp lay northwest of Tiande on the Poling River, more than eight thousand li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Their original royal camp stood northwest of Tiande on the Poling River, more than eight thousand li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 唐天寶中，安祿山犯闕，有助國討賊之功，累朝尚主，自號「天驕」，大爲唐朝之患。

translations.literal: In Tianbao of Tang, when An Lushan assaulted the palace, they had merit in aiding the state against rebels; successive dynasties married princesses to them; they styled themselves "Heaven's Pride" and became a great menace to the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao years, when An Lushan stormed the capital, they aided the Tang in suppressing the rebellion. Dynasty after dynasty bestowed imperial princesses upon them. They called themselves "Heaven's Pride" and became one of the Tang's gravest threats.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，其國爲黠戛斯所侵，部族擾亂，乃移帳至天德、振武間。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang their state was invaded by the Kirghiz, their tribes were thrown into disorder, and they moved their camps between Tiande and Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huichang era the Kirghiz overran their country, their tribes fell into turmoil, and they shifted their camps between Tiande and Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 時爲石雄、劉沔所襲，破之，復爲幽州節度使張仲武所攻，餘衆西奔，歸於吐蕃，吐蕃處之甘州，由是族帳微弱。

translations.literal: They were then attacked and defeated by Shi Xiong and Liu Mian, and again assaulted by Zhang Zhongwu, military governor of Youzhou; the remnant masses fled west and submitted to Tubo, which settled them in Ganzhou, and from this their tribal camps grew weak.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong and Liu Mian then struck and broke them, and Zhang Zhongwu, military governor of Youzhou, attacked them again. The survivors fled west and submitted to Tubo, which resettled them in Gan Prefecture. From that point their tribal power waned.

sentences.zh: 其後時通中國，世以中國爲舅，朝廷每賜書詔，亦常以甥呼之。

translations.literal: Thereafter they communicated with China from time to time; generation after generation they took China as maternal uncle, and whenever the court bestowed letters and edicts it also commonly addressed them as nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they maintained intermittent contact with China. Generation after generation they regarded the Chinese emperor as their maternal uncle, and the court, in its letters and edicts, habitually addressed them as nephew.

sentences.zh: 梁乾化元年十一月，遣都督周易言等入朝進貢，太祖御朝元殿引對，以易言爲右監門衛大將軍同正，以石壽兒、石論思並爲右千牛衛將軍同正，仍以左監門衛將軍楊沼充押領回鶻還蕃使，《五代會要》：以易言爲右監門衛大將軍同正，弟略麥之、石論思並爲左千牛衛將軍同正，李屋珠、安鹽山並爲右千牛衛將軍同正，仍以左鹽門衛上將軍楊沼爲左驍衛上將軍，充押領回鶻還番使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Qianhua under Liang, commissioner Zhou Yiyan and others were sent to court with tribute. Emperor Taizu received them in audience at Chaoyuan Hall. Yiyan was made Acting Right General-in-Chief of the Right Gate Guard, Shi Shou'er and Shi Lunci were both made Acting Generals of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, and Left Gate Guard General Yang Zhao was appointed envoy to escort the Uyghurs home. The Five Dynasties Essentials records: Yiyan was made Acting Right General-in-Chief of the Right Gate Guard; his younger brother Luemaizhi and Shi Lunci were both made Acting Generals of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard; Li Wuzhu and An Yanshan were both made Acting Generals of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard; and Left Gate Guard Senior General Yang Zhao was made Senior General of the Left Xiaowei Guard and appointed envoy to escort the Uyghurs home.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Qianhua under Liang, commissioner Zhou Yiyan and others came to court with tribute. Emperor Taizu received them in audience at Chaoyuan Hall, appointing Yiyan Acting Right General-in-Chief of the Right Gate Guard, Shi Shou'er and Shi Lunci Acting Generals of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, and Left Gate Guard General Yang Zhao envoy to escort the Uyghurs home. The Five Dynasties Essentials gives a fuller account: Yiyan as Acting Right General-in-Chief of the Right Gate Guard; his younger brother Luemaizhi and Shi Lunci as Acting Generals of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard; Li Wuzhu and An Yanshan as Acting Generals of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard; and Senior General Yang Zhao of the Left Gate Guard as Senior General of the Left Xiaowei Guard and envoy to escort the Uyghurs home.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人仇元通爲判官，厚賜繒帛，放令歸國，又賜其入朝僧凝盧、宜李思、宜延篯等紫衣。

translations.literal: Interpreting Investiture Attendant Qiu Yuantong served as clerk. Rich gifts of silk were bestowed, and they were sent home; the Buddhist monks who had come to court—Ninglu, Yi Lisi, Yi Yanfan, and others—were also granted purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: Interpreting Investiture Attendant Qiu Yuantong served as clerk. The court lavished silk gifts upon them and sent them home, and the Buddhist monks who had come to court—Ninglu, Yi Lisi, Yi Yanfan, and others—were granted purple robes.

sentences.zh: 後唐同光二年四月，其本國權知可汗仁美遣都督李引釋迦、副使鐵林、都監楊福安等共六十六人來貢方物，並獻善馬九匹。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Tongguang of Later Tang, their acting khan Renmei sent commissioner Li Yinshijia, vice-envoy Tielin, overseer Yang Fu'an, and sixty-six others in all to present local products and also offered nine fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Tongguang, acting khan Renmei sent commissioner Li Yinshijia, vice-envoy Tielin, overseer Yang Fu'an, and sixty-six others to present tribute, including nine fine horses.

sentences.zh: 莊宗召對於文明殿，乃命司農卿鄭績、將作少監何延嗣持節冊仁美爲英義可汗。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong received them in audience in the Hall of Civilizing Culture and ordered Minister of Agriculture Zheng Ji and Vice-Director of Imperial Works He Yansi to bear credentials and invest Renmei as Khan of Heroic Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong received them in audience in the Hall of Civilizing Culture and ordered Minister of Agriculture Zheng Ji and Vice-Director of Imperial Works He Yansi to invest Renmei as Khan of Heroic Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 至其年十一月，仁美卒，其弟狄銀嗣立，遣都督安千等朝貢。

translations.literal: By the eleventh month of that year Renmei had died; his younger brother Diyin succeeded and sent commissioner An Qian and others to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year Renmei died. His younger brother Diyin succeeded him and sent commissioner An Qian and others to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 狄銀卒，《歐陽史》：同光四年，狄銀卒。

translations.literal: Diyin died. The Ouyang History states: In the fourth year of Tongguang, Diyin died.
translations.idiomatic: Diyin died. The Ouyang History records that Diyin died in the fourth year of Tongguang.

sentences.zh: 阿咄欲立，亦遣使來貢名馬。

translations.literal: Atouyu succeeded and also sent envoys to present famous horses as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Atouyu succeeded and likewise sent envoys bearing famous horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 天成三年二月，其權知可汗仁裕遣都督李阿山等一百二十人入貢，明宗召對於崇元殿，賜物有差。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Tiancheng, acting khan Renyu sent commissioner Li Ashan and one hundred twenty others to present tribute; Mingzong received them in audience in the Hall of Exalted Origin and bestowed gifts in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year of Tiancheng, acting khan Renyu sent commissioner Li Ashan and one hundred twenty others with tribute. Mingzong received them in the Hall of Exalted Origin and bestowed gifts according to rank.

sentences.zh: 其年三月，命使冊仁裕爲順化可汗。

translations.literal: In the third month of that year envoys were ordered to invest Renyu as Khan of Compliant Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of that year envoys were dispatched to invest Renyu as Khan of Compliant Transformation.

sentences.zh: 四年，又遣都督掣撥等五人來朝，授掣撥等懷化司戈，遣命還蕃。

translations.literal: In the fourth year they again sent commissioner Chebo and five others to court; Chebo and the rest were appointed Huaihua Company Commanders and ordered to return to their realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year they sent commissioner Chebo and five others to court. Chebo and his companions were appointed Huaihua Company Commanders and ordered home.

sentences.zh: 長興元年十二月，遣使翟未思三十餘人，進馬八十匹、玉一團。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Changxing they sent envoy Zhai Weisi and more than thirty others, presenting eighty horses and one ball of jade.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Changxing they sent envoy Zhai Weisi and more than thirty others with eighty horses and a ball of jade.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，復遣都督李未等三十人來朝，進白鶻一聯，明宗召對於廣壽殿，厚加錫齎，仍命解放其鶻。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year they again sent commissioner Li Wei and thirty others to court, presenting a pair of white gyrfalcons; Mingzong received them in audience in the Hall of Broad Longevity, richly rewarded them, and also ordered the falcons released.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year they sent commissioner Li Wei and thirty others with a pair of white gyrfalcons. Mingzong received them in the Hall of Broad Longevity, lavished gifts upon them, and ordered the birds set free.

sentences.zh: 清泰二年七月，遣都督陳福海已下七十八人，進馬三百六十匹、玉二十團。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Qingtai they sent commissioner Chen Fuhai and seventy-eight others below him, presenting three hundred sixty horses and twenty balls of jade.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year of Qingtai they sent commissioner Chen Fuhai and seventy-eight subordinates with three hundred sixty horses and twenty balls of jade.

sentences.zh: 八月，敕回鶻朝貢使、密錄都督陳福海可懷化郎將，副使達奚相溫可懷化司階，監使屈密錄阿撥可歸德司戈，判官安均可懷化司戈。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict appointed Huihu tribute envoy and confidential recorder commissioner Chen Fuhai Huaihua Commandant, vice-envoy Daxi Xiangwen Huaihua Company Captain, overseer Qumilu Abo Guide Company Commander, and clerk An Jun Huaihua Company Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict named Huihu tribute envoy and confidential recorder Chen Fuhai Huaihua Commandant, vice-envoy Daxi Xiangwen Huaihua Company Captain, overseer Qumilu Abo Guide Company Commander, and clerk An Jun Huaihua Company Commander.

sentences.zh: 晉天福三年十月，遣使都督李萬全等朝貢，以萬全爲歸義大將軍，監使雷福德爲順化將軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Tianfu of Jin they sent commissioner Li Wanquan and others to court with tribute; Wanquan was made Great General of Returning Allegiance and overseer Lei Fude Compliant Transformation General.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year of Tianfu of Jin they sent commissioner Li Wanquan and others to court with tribute; Wanquan was made Great General of Returning Allegiance and overseer Lei Fude Compliant Transformation General.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，又遣都督拽里敦來朝，兼貢方物。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year they again sent commissioner Zhailidun to court, also presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year they sent commissioner Zhailidun to court again, bearing local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 其月，命衛尉卿邢德昭持節就冊爲奉化可汗。

translations.literal: That month Minister of the Guard Xing Dezhao was ordered to bear credentials on the spot and invest him as Khan of Reverent Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Minister of the Guard Xing Dezhao was sent with credentials to invest him as Khan of Reverent Transformation.

sentences.zh: 《歐陽史》：「晉高祖時，又加冊命，阿咄欲不知其爲狄銀親疏，亦不知其立卒，而仁裕訖五代常來朝貢，史亦失其紀。」

translations.literal: The Ouyang History states: "Under Emperor Gaozu of Jin additional investiture was granted; whether Atouyu was close or distant kin to Diyin is unknown, as are his accession and death, while Renyu came to court with tribute throughout the Five Dynasties—the histories also lose his record."
translations.idiomatic: The Ouyang History states: "Under Emperor Gaozu of Jin further investiture was granted. Whether Atouyu was near or distant kin to Diyin is unknown, as are the circumstances of his rise and death, whereas Renyu continued to send tribute throughout the Five Dynasties—yet the histories have lost the record of his reign as well."

sentences.zh: 五年正月，遣都督石海金等來貢良馬百駟，並白玉團、白玉鞍轡等，謝其封冊。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year they sent commissioner Shi Haijin and others to present one hundred teams of fine horses, together with white jade balls, white jade saddles and bridles, and the like, in thanks for their investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year they sent commissioner Shi Haijin and others with one hundred teams of fine horses, white jade balls, white jade saddles and bridles, and the like, to thank the court for their investiture.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐元年五月，遣使李屋等入朝貢馬並白玉、藥物等。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Qianyou of Han they sent envoy Li Wu and others to court, presenting horses together with white jade, medicines, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Qianyou under Later Han they sent envoy Li Wu and others to court with horses, white jade, medicines, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 七月，以入朝使李屋爲歸德大將軍，副使安鐵山、監使末相溫爲歸德將軍，判官翟毛哥爲懷化將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the court envoy Li Wu was made Great Guide General, vice-envoy An Tieshan and overseer Mo Xiangwen Guide Generals, and clerk Zhai Maoge Huaihua General.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month court envoy Li Wu was appointed Great Guide General, vice-envoy An Tieshan and overseer Mo Xiangwen Guide Generals, and clerk Zhai Maoge Huaihua General.

sentences.zh: 周廣順元年二月，遣使並摩尼貢玉團七十有七，白絺、貂皮、犛牛尾、藥物等。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Guangshun under Zhou, envoys together with the Manichaean mission presented seventy-seven jade balls, white silk, sable pelts, yak tails, medicines, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Guangshun under Zhou, envoys came with the Manichaean mission bearing seventy-seven jade balls, white silk, sable pelts, yak tails, medicines, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 先是，晉、漢已來，回鶻每至京師，禁民以私市易，其所有寶貨皆鬻之入官，民間市易者罪之。

translations.literal: Previously, from Jin and Han onward, whenever the Uyghurs reached the capital private trade with the populace was forbidden; all their valuables had to be sold to the government, and private traders were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, from the Jin and Han dynasties onward, whenever Uyghur missions reached the capital the people were forbidden to trade with them privately. All their valuables had to be sold to the government, and anyone who traded privately was punished.

sentences.zh: 至是，周太祖命除去舊法，每回鶻來者，聽私下交易，官中不得禁詰，由是玉之價直十損七八。

translations.literal: At this point Emperor Taizu of Zhou ordered the old regulations abolished: whenever Uyghurs came, private trade was permitted and officials might not prohibit or interrogate them; from this the price of jade fell by seven or eight tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Emperor Taizu of Zhou abolished the old rules. Whenever Uyghurs came, private trade was allowed and officials were forbidden to interfere. As a result the price of jade fell by seven or eight tenths.

sentences.zh: 顯德六年二月，又遣使朝貢，獻玉並碙砂等物，皆不納，所入馬量給價錢。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Xiande they again sent envoys to court, presenting jade, ammoniac, and other goods; all were refused, and for horses brought in payment was given by measure.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year of Xiande they sent envoys again with jade, ammoniac, and other goods. The court refused them all and paid only for the horses they accepted.

sentences.zh: 時世宗以玉雖稱寶，無益國用，故因而卻之。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Shizong held that although jade was called a treasure, it did not benefit state needs, and therefore rejected it on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong held that although jade was prized as treasure it did not serve the needs of state, and on that account he refused it.

sentences.zh: 高麗，本扶餘之別種。

translations.literal: Goryeo was originally a separate branch of Fuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo was originally an offshoot of Fuyu.

sentences.zh: 其國都平壤城，即漢樂浪郡之故地，在京師東四千餘里。

translations.literal: Its capital was Pyongyang, the former territory of Han's Lelang commandery, more than four thousand li east of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital was Pyongyang, on the site of the Han Lelang commandery, more than four thousand li east of the Chinese capital.

sentences.zh: 東渡海至於新羅，西北渡遼水至於營州，南渡海至於百濟，北至靺鞨，東西三千一百里，南北二千里。

translations.literal: East across the sea lay Silla; northwest across the Liao River lay Yingzhou; south across the sea lay Baekje; north to the Mohe—three thousand one hundred li east to west and two thousand li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: To the east lay Silla across the sea; to the northwest Ying Prefecture across the Liao River; to the south Baekje across the sea; to the north the Mohe. The realm measured three thousand one hundred li from east to west and two thousand li from north to south.

sentences.zh: 其官大者號大對盧，比一品，總知國事，三年一代，若稱職者不拘年限；

translations.literal: Their highest office was called Grand Tolu, equivalent to first rank, overseeing all state affairs, replaced every three years, though if competent the term was not fixed;
translations.idiomatic: Their highest minister was titled Grand Tolu, equivalent to first rank, with overall charge of state affairs. The post rotated every three years, though a capable holder might serve longer.

sentences.zh: 對盧已下官總十二級。

translations.literal: Below the Tolu there were twelve grades of office in all.
translations.idiomatic: Below the Tolu there were twelve grades of office in all.

sentences.zh: 外置州縣六十餘，大城置傉薩一人，比都督；

translations.literal: Beyond this more than sixty prefectures and counties were established; in large cities one Nusa was placed, equivalent to a military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: More than sixty prefectures and counties were established in the provinces. Large cities had a Nusa, equivalent to a military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 小城置道使一人，比刺史；

translations.literal: in small cities one daoshi was placed, equivalent to a prefect;
translations.idiomatic: Small cities had a daoshi, equivalent to a prefect.

sentences.zh: 其下各有僚佐，分曹掌事。

translations.literal: beneath them were assistants in each case, divided into bureaus to manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Each had subordinates divided into bureaus to handle affairs.

sentences.zh: 其王以白羅爲冠，白皮小帶，咸以金飾。

translations.literal: Their king wore a white silk cap and a narrow white-leather belt, all ornamented with gold.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a white silk cap and a narrow white-leather belt, both adorned with gold.

sentences.zh: 唐貞觀末，太宗伐之，不能下。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguan of Tang, Taizong attacked them but could not subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhenguan era, Taizong campaigned against them but could not bring them down.

sentences.zh: 至總章初，高宗命李勣率軍征之，遂拔其城，分其地爲郡縣。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Zongzhang, Gaozong ordered Li Ji to lead an army against them, took their capital, and divided their land into commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zongzhang era, Gaozong ordered Li Ji to lead an expedition, captured their capital, and carved their territory into commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 及唐之末年，中原多事，其國遂自立君長，前王姓高氏。

translations.literal: By the late years of Tang, with turmoil in the central plains, their state then established its own rulers; the former kings were of the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang dynasty neared its end and the central plains fell into turmoil, Goryeo reestablished its own rulers. The former royal house bore the surname Gao.

sentences.zh: 唐同光、天成中，累遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In Tongguang and Tiancheng of Tang they repeatedly sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongguang and Tiancheng eras they sent envoys to court with tribute on numerous occasions.

sentences.zh: 周顯德六年，高麗遣使貢紫白水晶二千顆。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xiande of Zhou, Goryeo sent envoys presenting two thousand purple and white crystal balls.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xiande under the Zhou, Goryeo sent envoys with two thousand purple and white crystal balls.

sentences.zh: 渤海靺鞨

translations.literal: Bohai Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: The Bohai Mohe.

sentences.zh: 渤海靺鞨，其俗呼其王爲可毒夫，對面呼聖，箋奏呼基下。

translations.literal: Among the Bohai Mohe, by custom they called their king Kedufu, addressed him as Sage face to face, and in memorials called him Jixia.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Bohai Mohe, custom held that the king was called Kedufu in ordinary speech, addressed as Sage in person, and styled Jixia in written memorials.

sentences.zh: 父曰老王，母曰太妃，妻曰貴妃，長子曰副王，諸子曰王子。

translations.literal: The father was called Old King, the mother Grand Consort, the wife Noble Consort, the eldest son Vice King, and other sons Princes.
translations.idiomatic: The father was styled Old King, the mother Grand Consort, the wife Noble Consort, the eldest son Vice King, and younger sons Princes.

sentences.zh: 世以大氏爲酋長。

translations.literal: Generation after generation the Da clan served as chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Generation after generation the Da clan held the chieftainship.

sentences.zh: 黑水靺鞨

translations.literal: Heishui Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: The Heishui Mohe.

sentences.zh: 黑水靺鞨，其俗尚質樸。

translations.literal: The Heishui Mohe valued plain simplicity in custom.
translations.idiomatic: The Heishui Mohe prized plain simplicity.

sentences.zh: 性猛悍，無憂戚，貴壯而賤老。

translations.literal: Their nature was fierce and bold; they knew no grief; they honored the strong and despised the old.
translations.idiomatic: They were fierce by nature, heedless of sorrow, honoring the strong and slighting the aged.

sentences.zh: 俗無文字，兵器有角弓楛失。

translations.literal: They had no writing by custom; their weapons included horn bows and wooden arrows.
translations.idiomatic: They had no written script. Their arms included horn bows and wooden-shafted arrows.

sentences.zh: 新羅，其國俗重九日相慶賀，每以是月拜日月之神。

translations.literal: In Silla, their national custom prized the Double Ninth for mutual celebration; each year in that month they worshipped the gods of sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: In Silla the people greatly honored the Double Ninth Festival for celebration, and in that month each year they worshipped the sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 婦人以髮繞頭，用彩及珠爲飾，髮甚鬒美。

translations.literal: Women wound their hair about the head and used colored silks and pearls as ornaments; their hair was very lustrous and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Women wound their hair about their heads and adorned it with colored silks and pearls. Their hair was remarkably thick and beautiful.

sentences.zh: 党項，其俗皆土著，居有棟宇，織毛罽以覆之。

translations.literal: The Tangut by custom were all settled cultivators; they dwelt in framed buildings and wove felt to cover them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut were settled people by custom. They lived in timber-framed dwellings roofed with woven felt.

sentences.zh: 尚武，其人多壽，至百五十、六十歲，不事生業，好爲盜賊。

translations.literal: They esteemed martial prowess; many lived long, to one hundred fifty or sixty years; they did not pursue livelihoods and delighted in banditry.
translations.idiomatic: They prized martial prowess. Many lived to one hundred fifty or even one hundred sixty years. They did not engage in regular livelihoods and were prone to raiding.

sentences.zh: 党項自同光以後，大姓之強者各自來朝貢。

translations.literal: From Tongguang onward the powerful great clans of the Tangut each came on their own to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tongguang era onward, powerful Tangut clans each came to court with tribute on their own.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，詔沿邊置場市馬，諸夷皆入市中國，有回鶻、党項馬最多。

translations.literal: Under Mingzong an edict ordered frontier horse markets established; all the Yi peoples entered the markets of China, with Huihu and Tangut horses the most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong the court ordered frontier horse markets established. Tribal peoples from every quarter came to trade within China, and Uyghur and Tangut horses were the most numerous.

sentences.zh: 明宗招懷遠人，馬來無駑壯皆集，而所售過常直，往來館給，道路倍費。

translations.literal: Mingzong sought to win over distant peoples; when horses came, weak and strong alike gathered, yet the prices paid exceeded the usual rate, with lodging and supplies along the road doubling the expense.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong sought to win over distant peoples. Whenever horses arrived, sound and unsound alike were purchased at prices above the usual rate, with lodging and supplies along the road doubling the cost.

sentences.zh: 其每至京師，明宗爲御殿見之，勞以酒食，既醉，連袂歌呼，道其土風以爲樂，去又厚以賜齎，歲耗百萬計。

translations.literal: Whenever they reached the capital, Mingzong received them in the imperial hall, entertained them with food and wine, and once drunk they linked arms singing and calling out, recounting their native customs for amusement; on departure they were again richly rewarded—annual expenditure ran to millions.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they reached the capital, Mingzong received them in the imperial hall and feasted them with food and wine. Once drunk, they would link arms, sing, and shout, recounting their native customs for amusement. On departure they were lavished with gifts again, and the annual cost ran into the millions.

sentences.zh: 唐大臣皆患之，數以爲言，乃詔吏就邊場售馬給直，止其來朝，而党項利其所得，來不可止。

translations.literal: Tang ministers all regarded this as a affliction and spoke of it repeatedly; an edict then ordered officials to buy horses and pay fair price at the frontier markets and stop their coming to court, yet the Tangut profited from what they gained and their coming could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Tang ministers regarded this as a serious burden and raised the matter repeatedly. An edict ordered officials to purchase horses at fair prices at the frontier markets and to end their visits to court. Yet the Tangut profited from the trade, and their visits could not be stopped.

sentences.zh: 其在靈、慶之間者，數犯邊爲盜。

translations.literal: Those between Ling and Qing repeatedly raided the border as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Those settled between Ling and Qing repeatedly raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 自河西回鶻朝貢中國，道其部落，輒邀劫之，執其使者，賣之他族以易牛馬。

translations.literal: When the Hexi Huihu came to court with tribute to China, passing through their tribes they were always waylaid; the envoys were seized and sold to other peoples to exchange for cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hexi Uyghurs came to court with tribute, their route passed through Tangut territory, where they were repeatedly ambushed. The Tangut seized the envoys and sold them to other tribes in exchange for cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 明宗遣靈武康福、邠州藥彥稠等出兵討之，福等擊破阿埋、韋悉、褒勒、強賴、埋廝骨尾及其大首領連香、李八薩王，都統悉那、埋摩，侍御乞埋、嵬悉逋等族。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong sent Kang Fu of Lingwu, Yao Yanchou of Binzhou, and others to campaign against them; Fu and the rest defeated the tribes of Amai, Weixi, Baole, Qianglai, Maisigui, and their great chieftains Lianxiang and Li Basawang, the commanders-in-chief Sina and Maimo, the attendants Qimai and Weisibu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong dispatched Kang Fu of Lingwu and Yao Yanchou of Bin Prefecture with troops to suppress them. Fu and his commanders broke the Amai, Weixi, Baole, Qianglai, and Maisigui tribes, together with their great chieftains Lianxiang and Li Basawang, commanders-in-chief Sina and Maimo, attendants Qimai and Weisibu, and other clans.

sentences.zh: 殺數千人，獲其牛羊巨萬計及其所劫外國寶玉等，悉以賜軍士，由是党項之患稍息。

translations.literal: They killed several thousand men, seized tens of thousands of their cattle and sheep and the foreign jades and gems they had plundered, and bestowed all on the soldiers; from this the Tangut menace subsided somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: They killed several thousand men and seized tens of thousands of cattle and sheep, together with the foreign jades and gems the Tangut had looted, distributing the spoils among the troops. Thereafter the Tangut threat eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 其他諸族，散處沿邊界上甚衆，然皆無國邑君長，故莫得而紀次云。

translations.literal: The other various peoples were numerous, scattered along the frontier borders, yet all lacked states, settlements, and ruling chiefs, and so none could be recorded in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Numerous other peoples were scattered along the frontier, yet none possessed states, settled domains, or recognized rulers, and so they cannot be recorded in any orderly sequence.

sentences.zh: 昆明部落

translations.literal: Kunming tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Kunming tribes.

sentences.zh: 昆明部落，其俗椎髻跣足。

translations.literal: Among the Kunming tribes, their custom was topknots and bare feet.
translations.idiomatic: The Kunming tribes wore their hair in topknots and went barefoot by custom.

sentences.zh: 酋長披虎皮，下者披氈。

translations.literal: Chieftains wore tiger pelts; those below wore felt.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftains draped themselves in tiger pelts; their subordinates wore felt.

sentences.zh: 于闐，其俗好事妖神。

translations.literal: In Yutian, their custom was to devote themselves to strange spirits and gods.
translations.idiomatic: In Yutian the people were devoted by custom to strange spirits and deities.

sentences.zh: 占城，本地鳥之大者有孔雀。

translations.literal: In Champa, among the large native birds there is the peacock.
translations.idiomatic: In Champa the largest native birds include the peacock.

sentences.zh: 牂牁蠻

translations.literal: Zangke Man.
translations.idiomatic: The Zangke Man.

sentences.zh: 牂牁蠻，其國法，劫盜者三倍還贓，殺人者出牛馬三十頭乃得贖死。

translations.literal: Among the Zangke Man, by their national law robbers had to return threefold the stolen goods, and killers had to pay thirty head of cattle and horses to redeem their lives from death.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Zangke Man, national law required robbers to restore stolen goods at triple value, and murderers to pay thirty head of cattle and horses to ransom their lives from execution.
